newsitem.title: USA: Conseco to purchase Transport Holdings.
newsitem.headline: Conseco to purchase Transport Holdings.

text.p: Conseco Inc and Transport Holdings Inc said Thursday they signed a merger agreement, under which Conseco would acquire Transport for $70 a share in Conseco common stock.
Transport provides cancer insurance and other supplemental health insurance products.

The total value of the transaction would be approximately $311 million, including $228 million to purchase Transport's 3.2 million common shares and equivalents and $83 million to retire bank debt and preferred stock, the companies said.

Under the agreement, each issued and outstanding share of Transport class A common stock would be converted into the right to receive Conseco common stock. The number of shares to be received would be determined by dividing $70 by the average closing price of Conseco common stock during the 10 trading days immediately preceding the second trading day prior to closing. The number of shares would not be more than 1.8301 nor less than 1.40, the companies said.
Transport's outstanding convertible debt, stock options and warrants, when converted or exercised, would receive the same ratio of Conseco shares.
The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of 1996, pending customary terms and conditions, including approval by Transport stockholders and regulatory approvals.
Under the agreement, Transport would be merged into Conseco, with Conseco being the surviving corporation.

The terms of the agreement also provide that, to the extent required by its fiduciary duties to Transport's shareholders, Transport's board may evaluate other offers. If Transport entered into another agreement or terminated the Conseco merger agreement because of another offer, Transport would be required to pay a break-up fee, the companies said.

Conseco Chairman Stephen Hilbert said his company's strategic objective is to be a leader in each of its major product lines, including supplemental health insurance, retirement savings annuities and universal life insurance.
"We are seeing more acquisition opportunities today than ever before," Hilbert said. "We remain very selective..."

He said Conseco is focusing exclusively on those acquisitions that complement its long-term business strategy, maintain earnings momentum and maintain a conservative capital structure, with debt no more than 35 percent of total capital.
Conseco has completed or announced six transactions so far in 1996.
Upon completion of the six transactions, Conseco said it will have $31 billion of investments under management and $27 billion of assets on its own balance sheet.

It also will have $7.0 billion of annual premiums and revenues, $4.8 billion of equity market capitalization and more than $690 million of projected annual earnings before interest and taxes cash flow. Total capital will approach $5.6 billion, it added.
